listed_building_title: Parish Church of St Serf, Dollar Road
statutory_title: Principal historic parish church, incorporating an earlier bell.
documented_date: Built 1827–1829; hall added 1889; interior recast 1920; bell dated 1670

listed_building_title: Tower of Former Popular Institute, Ochil Street
statutory_title: Surviving clock tower and gable of the former Popular Institute.
documented_date: Clock tower added in 1879; former Popular Institute built 1859 and demolished 1986

listed_building_title: 99 High Street, Former Municipal Buildings and Library
statutory_title: Classical early-19th-century civic building later used as municipal offices and library.
Principal surviving service building of the former Tillicoultry House estate.

listed_building_title: Bridge over Tillicoultry Burn at Clock Mill
statutory_title: Stone bridge associated with the Clock Mill and burnside industry.
documented_date: Probably early 19th century, likely associated with the 1824 Clock Mill

statutory_title: Old parish churchyard containing early gravestones and the pre-Reformation church site.
documented_date: Church site from the 12th century; 16th- and 17th-century stones include a headstone dated 1723

listed_building_title: Former J & D Paton's Woollen Mill, Weavers Way
statutory_title: Major surviving element of Tillicoultry's woollen industry.
documented_date: Firm founded 1824; mill begun 1836; converted to housing in the late 1980s

statutory_title: Intact Art Deco entertainment hall associated with the Devonvale Mills welfare programme.
